requirements.observation: Common credential format; equivalent online/offline assurance and privacy, not merely common syntax.

cases.constructed: Issuer, wallet and verifier pass separate synthetic checks against the same profile version
cases.proposed_evidence: Require actual paired interaction evidence, applicable role-specific obligations and matching profile version; separately evaluate privacy, status freshness, and service outcomes. Do not turn same-profile declaration into demonstrated interoperability.

cases.constructed: Two individually conforming actors use different profile versions or incompatible hook resolutions
cases.proposed_evidence: Inspect exact profile identifier/version, normative references, hook resolutions, criteria mappings and applicable vectors. Test incompatibility and safe refusal; no assumption of cross-profile interoperability or downgrade permission.

cases.constructed: A technically successful profile is presented as approved despite missing evidence of rulemaking
cases.proposed_evidence: Inspect the rulemaking docket, publication and response records and Department approval. Treat missing records as unknown; distinguish technical suitability, approval and actual certification.

cases.constructed: Audit-ready logging is used to collect individually linkable presentation records
cases.proposed_evidence: Inspect record scope, access and retention against anti-surveillance protections and audit purpose; verify evidence can be produced without expanding forbidden monitoring. Separate program operational audit from presentation history.

cases.constructed: Passing automated tests coexist with absent expert assessment or conflicting administrative records
cases.proposed_evidence: Keep method applicability, observations and evidence dates separate; preserve missing or contradictory evidence. INT-01 marks EXPT N/A yet describes an expert-review need in its limitation; ask for clarification, not silently modify the matrix. Test unauthorized promotion of partial results.

cases.constructed: Common format passes online and offline encoding tests but privacy or assurance differs by mode
cases.proposed_evidence: Check each mode independently for selective disclosure, unlinkability, predicate proofs and equivalent assurance; cross-reference offline status constraints. Successful decoding alone is insufficient.

observations: Base conformance is mandatory; profile conformance binds technology choices and supports interoperability within the same profile.
Conformance chapter identifies issuer, wallet and verifier/RP types, and refers to Annex E for full per-requirement obligations.

Profiles must include identifier/version, normative references, hook resolution, evaluation-criterion mapping, profile-specific requirements and test vectors or reference implementations where applicable.
Department approval proceeds through rulemaking; multiple profiles may coexist.
Evaluation methodology includes document review, architecture analysis, functional testing, security assessment, interoperability testing and privacy analysis.
Guide does not establish a certification program; certification guidance is prospective.

Base-conformance text names Parts 1–8 and annexes while actor-specific types include applicable Part 9 CRY/PRV/INT requirements; clarify how all applicable cross-cutting requirements, including KMS/ORG, enter base conformance. Do not infer exemption.
framework.candidate_aggregation_rule: No overall PASS inferred from document completeness, individual component results, partial method coverage, common format or a profile label. Retain unknown, stale, contradictory and out-of-scope evidence separately; accountable review required.

limitations: No actual profiles, approval dockets, certification artifacts or operational evidence examined.
No independent legal conclusion, risk scoring or verified guardrail.
